# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute: The bomb shows a red light and display 0. There are three wires. Left is yellow, center is blue, right is red.

I have received information from Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb: Red light, Display 0. Wires are Yellow (left), Blue (center), Red (right).
Mute has not spoken yet (or I didn't hear them? No, Mute cannot speak. Mute must gesture or I need to ask Mute for manual info).
Wait, the context says "Deaf says: ...". This implies Deaf sent a message that reached me? But Deaf cannot speak. And I am Blind, so I cannot see gestures. How did I receive this?
Ah, looking at the previous turn's output: `speak(to="mute", text="...")`. That went to Mute.
The new arrival is "Deaf says: ...". This is strange. Deaf cannot speak. Unless the system translates gestures to text for me? Or maybe Deaf *did* speak and I can hear? No, rules say Deaf cannot hear, but doesn't explicitly say Deaf cannot speak? Table: Deaf "Cannot Hear anything, or touch the bomb". It does NOT say Deaf cannot speak. It says Deaf "Can See".
If Deaf can speak, then Deaf's speech reaches whoever can hear. I (Blind) can hear. So I received Deaf's speech.
Okay, so Deaf told us: Light=Red, Display=0, Wires=Yellow(1), Blue(2), Red(3).

Now I need Mute's help. Mute reads the manual. Mute cannot speak. Mute must gesture.
I (Blind) cannot see gestures.
So how do I get info from Mute?
I can't see Mute's gestures. Mute can't speak.
This seems like a deadlock unless I can interpret something else or if Mute has another way to communicate.
Wait, "Speech is a voice... Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that gesture while you talk."
Maybe Mute can write text? No, Mute "Cannot Speak".
Is there a channel I'm missing?
"You never receive gesture." -> Confirmed, I don't get Mute's gestures directly.
But if Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf speaks to me?
Or if I ask Deaf to relay Mute's gestures?
Deaf can see Mute's gestures. Deaf can speak to me.
So the chain is: Mute (Gestures) -> Deaf (Sees) -> Deaf (Speaks) -> Me (Hears).

Currently, I know the visual state from Deaf. I need the manual instructions.
I should ask Deaf to watch Mute and tell me what Mute says/gestures regarding the manual.
Since I just spoke to Mute in Turn 1 asking for help, Mute might be gesturing now. But I haven't heard from Deaf about Mute yet.
I will speak to Deaf, asking them to observe Mute and report any manual instructions related to the current state (Red Light, 0, Y/B/R wires).

```
speak(to="deaf", text="Please watch Mute closely. If Mute gestures any instructions from the manual about the red light, display 0, or the yellow/blue/red wires, please speak them to me immediately.")
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Light is now yellow. Wires are unchanged: left is yellow, middle is blue, right is red.

The light has changed from red to yellow. The wires remain Yellow (left/1), Blue (middle/2), Red (right/3).
I previously tried to speak to Deaf, but the system said "Nobody could receive that". This is confusing because Deaf just spoke to me. Why did my speech not reach them?
Ah, looking at the rules: "Whoever can hear receives your words". Deaf *cannot* hear. So I cannot `speak` to Deaf. My previous attempt failed because Deaf is deaf.
I need Mute's instructions. Mute reads the manual. Mute cannot speak. Mute must gesture.
Deaf can see gestures. Deaf can speak.
So I must ask Deaf to watch Mute and tell me what Mute is gesturing.
But I can't speak to Deaf.
Wait, if I can't speak to Deaf, and Deaf can't hear me, how do I communicate with Deaf?
"Your channels split the room... in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and gesture a different thing to Deaf".
Okay, so I **gesture** to Deaf.
Deaf sees my gestures. Deaf can then relay info to Mute? No, Mute can't hear Deaf either? Mute can hear.
Let's trace the communication graph again.
- Me (Blind): Can Hear (receives Speech). Can Touch. Can Speak (to those who hear: Mute, Blind?). Can Gesture (to those who see: Deaf, Mute?).
    - Rules say: "When you speak, Mute receives it." -> Implies Mute can hear.
    - Rules say: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." -> Implies Deaf and Mute can see.
- Deaf: Can See. Cannot Hear.
    - Receives Gestures from Me/Mute.
    - Sends Gestures to Me? No, I don't receive gestures.
    - Sends Speech? No, nobody hears Deaf? Wait. "Whoever can hear receives your words". If Deaf speaks, only those who can hear receive it. Who can hear? Mute and Blind (me). So Deaf CAN speak to me!
    - But in Turn 3, my `speak(to="deaf")` failed. Why? Because Deaf cannot HEAR. Correct.
    - So Deaf can SPEAK to me (because I can hear). But I cannot SPEAK to Deaf (because they can't hear).
    - To talk to Deaf, I must GESTURE.

Current State:
Light: Yellow.
Wires: 1(Yellow), 2(Blue), 3(Red).
Display: Unknown (Deaf didn't mention it changing, or maybe it's still 0? Or unknown).

I need the manual instruction for this state.
Mute has the manual.
I need to get Mute to give the instruction.
How do I ask Mute? I can `speak` to Mute.
In Turn 1, I spoke to Mute. Did Mute respond? We haven't seen a response from Mute yet.
Maybe Mute is waiting for more specific info or didn't understand?
Or maybe Mute is trying to gesture to Deaf, and Deaf hasn't translated it to me yet?
Deaf just told me the light changed. Deaf is active.

Strategy:
1. Ask Mute directly via speech for the rule regarding "Yellow Light, Display ?, Wires Y/B/R".
2. Since I don't know the display value, I should probably ask Deaf (via gesture) to confirm the display value first? Or just ask Mute to look up based on the light/wires and whatever display is current?
Actually, Deaf didn't mention the display in the last message. It might be unchanged (0) or hidden.
Let's assume the display is still relevant.
I will speak to Mute asking for the cut instruction for a bomb with Yellow Light, and wires Yellow/Blue/Red. I'll also ask Mute to clarify if the display matters and what it says if they can see it? No, Mute reads the manual, doesn't see the bomb. Deaf sees the bomb.

So:
1. I need Deaf to tell me the Display value. I must **gesture** to Deaf to ask for it.
   - What gesture means "What is the display number?"
   - I don't have a predefined dictionary. I need to establish one or use common sense.
   - Maybe I can just gesture "Question" or point to the display area? I can't point visually.
   - Alternative: I can ask Mute to listen for Deaf's speech? No, Mute can hear Deaf.
   - If I speak to Mute: "Ask Deaf to report the display value."
   - Mute can't speak. Mute can gesture to Deaf.
   - Deaf sees Mute's gesture. Deaf reports to me.

This seems long. Let's try to shortcut.
Deaf already spoke to me about the light. Deaf knows I am listening.
If I gesture to Deaf, Deaf will see it.
What if I just wait for Deaf to volunteer the display? Unlikely.

Let's try speaking to Mute again, very clearly.
"I need the manual instruction for cutting wires when the light is YELLOW. The wires are Left=Yellow, Middle=Blue, Right=Red. Please check the manual for this configuration. Also, please signal to Deaf to tell me the current DISPLAY value."

And I should gesture to Deaf to acknowledge I'm ready or to ask for the display?
Since I don't know the gesture language, I'll stick to speech to Mute, hoping Mute can direct Deaf or provide the answer if the display isn't critical or if Mute infers it.

However, there is a risk. If the manual requires the display value, I'm stuck without it.
Let's try to establish a simple code with Deaf via gestures? Too slow.
Better: Use Mute as the intermediary for logic, Deaf for data.

Message to Mute:
"The light is now YELLOW. Wires are 1:Yellow, 2:Blue, 3:Red. I need to know which wire to cut according to the manual. Please indicate the correct wire position (1, 2, or 3) by gesturing to Deaf, so Deaf can tell me. Also, ask Deaf to confirm the DISPLAY value."

This puts the burden on Mute to formulate the request to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The light is now YELLOW. Wires are 1:Yellow, 2:Blue, 3:Red. Please check the manual for this state. Indicate the correct wire to cut (1, 2, or 3) by gesturing to Deaf. Also, please signal Deaf to report the current DISPLAY value to me.")
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is yellow. There are three wires. Cut the one on your far right.

Deaf has provided a direct instruction: "Cut the one on your far right."
Based on Deaf's previous description, the wires are arranged Left (Yellow), Middle (Blue), Right (Red).
"Far right" corresponds to Wire 3.
I am Blind and can touch the bomb. I should execute this action.
Before cutting, I will confirm with Mute if this aligns with the manual for the current state (Yellow Light, Display unknown/0, Wires Y/B/R) just in case Deaf is guessing or misinterpreting, but since Deaf is the only one who sees the bomb and Mute hasn't signaled otherwise, and Deaf gave a clear command, I will proceed. However, safety first: I will cut wire 3 as instructed by the visual observer.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
